summary: Three small layout fixes to the prerendered marketing site. (1) The footer drops its fourth, unlabeled column of page links, leaving three groups: brand, Services and Company. On desktop they sit in a 3-track grid (2fr 1fr 1fr) and stack on phones. (2) /contact gets the same navy page-header band as the other inner pages (eyebrow CONTACT, h1, lead and the 'Prefer email?' mailto line), with the form and 'What happens next' card in a normal section below it. (3) The /systems hero puts the text (about 40%) and the architecture diagram (about 60%, vertically centered) side by side from 1024px up, and stacks them on phones. The diagram itself is unchanged.
steps: Read the existing acceptance tests first, especially layout-render, review-fixes-render, systems-render, hydrated-contact-submit, navigation-render and prerender-render. Keep them passing. Don't change any copy, hrefs, ids, ARIA or diagram content beyond what is listed here.

Footer (src/components/Footer.tsx, plus footer data in src/content/site.ts if it lives there): delete the fourth column (the Services/Systems/Training/Engagements/About/Contact page-link list) entirely, including its markup and data use. Keep exactly three groups inside the footer grid element (e.g. class `footer-grid`).
Footer group 1 (brand): the wordmark, the line 'AI enablement, training and custom development.' and the mailto:hello@thebayesgroup.com link.
Footer group 2: the h2 'Services' with links in this order: AI Enablement, Training, Custom Development, Systems engineering, Engagements.
Footer group 3: the h2 'Company' with links About (/about) and Contact (/contact).
Footer headings: 'Services' and 'Company' are the only headings in the footer. Every link in the footer sits in one of the three groups.

Footer bottom row: '© 2026 The Bayes Group' sits below the grid, outside the three groups, after a hairline. Keep the `<nav aria-label="Footer">` landmark. If it wraps the two link columns, make the 3-track grid still work, e.g. with `display: contents` on the nav, or by putting the grid class on an element whose three children are the groups.

Footer CSS (global.css): the footer grid is a single column (stacked, 32px gap) by default. Inside `@media (min-width: 1024px)` it uses `grid-template-columns: 2fr 1fr 1fr`, with the wordmark group first and widest. Remove any 4-track footer grid rule (no `repeat(4, …)` or 4-value grid-template-columns on any footer class).

Contact page (src/pages/ContactPage.tsx): wrap the page header in its own first section in main, reusing the exact same page-header band component/classes that Services/Systems/Training/Engagements/About use. That means navy background via var(--color-navy) and the data-grid motif (aria-hidden svg) if those pages render it.

Contact band content: the `.eyebrow` 'Contact' (shown uppercase), the h1 'Book a consultation' (white), the lead "Tell us what you're working on and we'll reply within one business day." and the line 'Prefer email? hello@thebayesgroup.com'. The email stays an `<a href="mailto:hello@thebayesgroup.com">` styled light (#5FC4C4 or white) on navy.

Contact body: the band contains no form. The two-column form plus the 'What happens next' card follow in a separate normal section (usual section padding) below. Keep exactly one h1 on the page, and leave the form ids, labels and behavior untouched.

Systems hero (src/pages/SystemsPage.tsx): inside the hero, wrap the content in one grid element (e.g. class `systems-hero__grid`) with exactly two children: a text column holding the eyebrow (if any), the h1 and the lead `

`, followed by a diagram column holding `` (or whichever variant is used now). The text column comes first in the DOM.

Systems hero CSS: the grid's base rule has no multi-column grid-template-columns, so phones stack it with the diagram below. Inside `@media (min-width: 1024px)` it gets `grid-template-columns: minmax(0, 2fr) minmax(0, 3fr)` and `align-items: center`. Don't modify ArchitectureDiagram.tsx.

Update DESIGN.md: Footer is 3 columns (brand 2fr | Services | Company); the Contact page has a navy header band; the Systems hero puts the diagram beside the text (text 2fr | diagram 3fr) on desktop. Keep `npm run build` (prerender) working.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Runs the app's acceptance tests: the Jest files in __tests__/acceptance/. Generated by the pipeline; the tests
themselves are locked files written by the planner. ACCEPTANCE_MILESTONE=N runs only the tests of milestones 1..N."""
import json
import os
import subprocess
import sys

here = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
os.chdir(here)
if not os.path.isdir("node_modules"):
    lock = os.path.exists("package-lock.json")
    subprocess.run(["npm", "ci" if lock else "install", "--include=dev", "--no-audit", "--no-fund"], check=False, timeout=1500)
cmd = ["npx", "jest", "--ci", "__tests__/acceptance"]
m = os.environ.get("ACCEPTANCE_MILESTONE", "")
if m.isdigit():
    cmd += ["-t", "^(" + "|".join("M%d" % i for i in range(1, int(m) + 1)) + "): "]
# The app's own test script may add node flags (e.g. --experimental-vm-modules): use the same ones.
try:
    script = json.load(open("package.json")).get("scripts", {}).get("test", "")
except (OSError, ValueError):
    script = ""
env = dict(os.environ)
if "--experimental-vm-modules" in script:
    env["NODE_OPTIONS"] = (env.get("NODE_OPTIONS", "") + " --experimental-vm-modules").strip()
print("Running: " + " ".join(cmd), flush=True)
sys.exit(subprocess.run(cmd, env=env, timeout=1500).returncode)
